After the astronauts finish their investigation, when they take a spacecraft to return from Mars to Earth, they undergo the orbital transfer process shown in the figure. Then regarding this spacecraft, which of the following statements is correct (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When the spacecraft moves on orbit II, its speed when passing point P is greater than its speed when passing point Q
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, multiple dashed orbits are drawn near the central celestial body “Mars”, labeled orbit I, orbit II, and orbit III. Orbit II is an elliptical orbit. The point P through which the spacecraft passes on orbit II is located on the right side of Mars, at a position relatively close to Mars; point Q is located on the left side of Mars, obviously farther from Mars. Then reason: When the spacecraft moves on the same elliptical orbit II, the semimajor axis of the orbit is fixed. According to the velocity law of elliptical orbits, the closer it is to the central celestial body Mars, the smaller the gravitational potential energy, the greater the kinetic energy, and the greater the velocity; the farther it is from Mars, the smaller the velocity. Since in the figure the distance from point P to Mars is less than the distance from point Q to Mars, namely r_P < r_Q, therefore v_P > v_Q. Conclusion: The spacecraft’s velocity when passing point P is greater than its velocity when passing point Q.
